kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
locale: en
buttonLabel: "Explore the culture of Brazil, Colombia and Peru"
lead: >-
  Brazil, Peru and Colombia reveal South American history through three very different sets of landmarks: Rio de Janeiro's urban landscape, Inca heritage in Cusco and Machu Picchu, and Cartagena's colonial neighbourhoods and Bogotá's museums. On Ada Tours' existing programme, these places belong to a long eight-country route. When choosing, consider not only the attractions' names but also the actual excursion days, altitude and flights between them.
---

## From Rio to Machu Picchu and Cartagena: which periods does the itinerary cover?

**The most extensive archaeological section of this combination is in Peru.** Travelling from Puno to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), visitors discover Andean communities and ancient structures. In Cusco, the programme includes Coricancha, Sacsayhuamán, Qenqo, Puka Pukara and Tambomachay. A full day is then devoted to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). UNESCO considers the site one of the great achievements of Inca architecture and planning, with stone terraces closely integrated into the surrounding mountains.

Brazil offers a different historical narrative. In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the programme includes Corcovado with the Christ the Redeemer statue, along with tours of Sugarloaf Mountain and the city. Views of the mountains and bay show how the metropolis developed between the coast and steep slopes. [Rio's Metropolitan Cathedral](/brazil/place/rio-metropolitan-cathedral/) is an example of modern urban architecture; these excursions focus more on the city and its symbols than on archaeology.

Colombia combines colonial history with museum collections and contemporary city life. In [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), the itinerary visits fortifications, old neighbourhoods and San Felipe de Barajas Fortress. UNESCO recognises Cartagena as an important example of sixteenth-to-eighteenth-century maritime defence systems and a historic Caribbean port. In [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), the programme includes La Candelaria, the Gold Museum, the Botero Collection and Monserrate. A separate day is devoted to Zipaquirá's Salt Cathedral.

## How the sightseeing days are organised

On the actual [32-day journey through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), Rio opens the itinerary: two sightseeing programmes explore the city's symbols and central neighbourhoods. Peru appears around the middle, after Chile and Bolivia, with Puno, Cusco, Machu Picchu and [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). In Lima, the excursion travels from Miraflores to the historic centre, including its squares and cathedrals. Lima's historic centre is associated with the Spanish viceroyalty and is recognised by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site.

The Colombian section concludes the journey. Before Cartagena, travellers visit Medellín, [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/) and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/), known for the painted façades of its houses. Bogotá and Zipaquirá follow Cartagena. This order allows comparisons between different forms of urban heritage, but **other countries on the itinerary** lie between Brazil and Colombia. That matters when planning trip duration and flights.

This selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The [general Brazil, Colombia and Peru catalogue](/multi-country/brazil_colombia_peru/) also lists trips with other interests; [multi-country cultural and historical programmes](/multi-country/interests/culture-and-history/) allow you to choose a different combination of countries.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## How the three cultural sections differ

| Country | Main focus |
|---|---|
| Brazil | The city, bay and architecture of Rio |
| Peru | The Incas, Cusco, Machu Picchu and Lima |
| Colombia | Cartagena, Bogotá and Zipaquirá |

In [Peru](/peru/), historic sites are closely connected with Andean geography: some monuments are at considerable altitude, and the road from Puno to Cusco crosses mountain regions. Machu Picchu is visited on a day excursion with a train journey, not as a hike along the Inca Trail. Other options can be found among [Peru's cultural tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/peru/).

In [Brazil](/brazil/), the cultural section of the selected journey is relatively short and concentrated in Rio. To explore the country's historic cities in greater depth, select a suitable programme from [Brazil's cultural and historical tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/brazil/) rather than assuming all those places are included on the 32-day journey.

In [Colombia](/colombia/), an interesting comparison is between Cartagena's Spanish fortifications and Bogotá's pre-Hispanic collections. Historic neighbourhoods are visited with a guide, while museum days depend on institutional opening schedules. [Colombia's cultural itineraries](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/colombia/) offer opportunities to allocate more time to these cities.

## Planning history-focused travel without overloading the itinerary

If Inca archaeology is the main goal, allowing time for altitude and museums in Cusco matters more than the number of countries. On the existing tour, Cusco follows Puno, so travellers have already spent time at altitude, but acclimatisation and tolerance of physical demands still differ individually. A flight to Lima after sightseeing in Cusco adds another change of conditions.

Museum schedules are important in Colombia. The programme notes that Bogotá's Gold Museum is closed on Mondays, while the Mint Museum and Botero Collection are closed on Tuesdays. Changes to flight times may therefore affect the sightseeing day. Weather varies as well: coastal Cartagena, high-altitude Bogotá and the Peruvian Andes call for different clothing.

We help organise the visit sequence, coordinate guides and flights, and decide which cultural stops to retain on a private route. A shorter journey covering only Brazil, Peru and Colombia requires a new calculation of duration and included services; the existing eight-country programme cannot be relabelled as a three-country tour without changes.

## Frequently asked questions about the culture and history of Brazil, Peru and Colombia

### Is Machu Picchu included on the featured tour?

Yes. The programme includes a full-day excursion with an English-speaking guide, a train journey and a return to Cusco. It is one of the main cultural and historical stops on the entire route.

### Will we see colonial Lima and Cartagena?

Yes. Lima has a sightseeing excursion around the historic centre, while Cartagena includes a walk through old neighbourhoods and an introduction to its fortifications. Visits to particular museums depend on each day's itinerary.

### What should I consider when visiting Bogotá's museums?

Their closing days. According to the programme, the Gold Museum is closed on Mondays, while the Mint Museum and Botero Collection are closed on Tuesdays. These arrangements should be checked again if the timetable changes.

### Can I choose only the cultural section without travelling to eight countries?

Yes, as a private request. A new itinerary covering Rio, Peru and Colombia's cities would need to be designed, with flights, duration and excursions agreed separately. The existing programme visits eight nations.

buttonLabel: "Explore nature in Brazil, Colombia and Peru"
lead: >-
  Iguazu Falls, high-altitude Lake Titicaca and the Peruvian Andes, and the green hills around Guatapé in Colombia are all included in one extensive South American itinerary. We explain how much time is devoted to nature, why Machu Picchu belongs to the cultural programme and how to account for altitude and long flights.
---

## Nature in Brazil, Peru and Colombia: from waterfalls to the Andes

Our [Brazil–Colombia–Peru selection](/multi-country/brazil_colombia_peru/) includes journeys with these three countries as main destinations. Among our nature itineraries you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}: a [32-day journey through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). The programme also covers Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Ecuador. “Brazil, Peru and Colombia” thus describes a confirmed **country combination within a much larger journey**, not a direct transfer between three stops.

The natural appeal of this selection lies in the contrast between Iguazu Falls, the high-altitude landscapes around Lake Titicaca and the scenery around Guatapé. In Peru, the route also includes Andean archaeological monuments, particularly [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). Although it lies among mountains, its scheduled visit is primarily cultural and historical, not a separate mountaineering or trekking stage.

## Brazil: a day at Iguazu and the other side across the border

After São Paulo and [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the route continues to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). On the Brazilian side, travellers see panoramic views of the waterfalls during a group excursion with a Russian-speaking guide. The following day is devoted to the Argentine side, after which a flight to Buenos Aires is scheduled.

The two sides offer different viewpoints. For this stage, take footwear suited to wet walkways, protect electronic equipment from spray and allow time for the border crossing. The Bird Park and Macuco Safari are listed as **optional paid activities**; their proximity to Iguazu does not mean they are included in the standard tour price.

To compare shorter and longer journeys, see [nature tours in Brazil](/interests/nature/tours/brazil/). Some focus on the waterfalls while others may include additional natural regions; what matters is the published itinerary, not just a broad thematic label.

## Peru: Titicaca and Cusco's mountain geography

Peru follows the Chilean and Bolivian stages. During the journey from La Paz via Tiwanaku to Puno, the route reaches the [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) region and the floating Uros Islands. This high-altitude lake combines a striking natural environment with the lives of local communities.

An overland transfer to Cusco follows, then a visit to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), an excursion to Inca monuments and a flight to Lima. Machu Picchu is explored on an organised sightseeing day. **A multi-day trek along Inca trails is not specified**, and the nature label should not create that expectation.

Altitude is a significant practical factor: before Peru, travellers cross Bolivia's highlands, while Peru adds Titicaca and Cusco. Physical demands and wellbeing change considerably between these stops and Brazil's lowlands. Agree on a sensible pace with regard to individual altitude tolerance, medical advice and transfer schedules.

## Colombia: Guatapé as a scenic rather than wilderness stage

After Peru, the extended tour visits Ecuador before reaching Medellín. For nature enthusiasts, the excursion to [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and El Peñón rock is especially memorable, with views of the reservoir and green hills. The day combines a scenic stop with a visit to a town.

Cartagena and [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) follow, with mainly city excursions. The published Colombian section does not contain a dedicated hike through a national park or an extensive wildlife-watching programme. If a nature reserve is your priority, review [other nature itineraries in Colombia](/interests/nature/tours/colombia/).

Colombia therefore broadens the range of landscapes in this three-country selection, but the experience differs from an expedition through undisturbed wilderness.

## Choosing priorities and a realistic duration

| Stop | Main reason to include it |
|---|---|
| Iguazu | The waterfall system |
| Titicaca | High-altitude lake |
| Machu Picchu | Inca history amid the Andes |
| Guatapé | Rock and reservoir |

If you want to visit all four in sequence, you must also account for the intermediate countries and days on the complete published itinerary. In particular, Bolivia follows Chile, while Ecuador follows Peru before the journey reaches Colombia. There is no direct Peru–Colombia flight on the programme described; this section cannot be disregarded without redesigning the trip.

Ada Tours helps decide where a sightseeing excursion is sufficient and where more time is worthwhile, coordinate flights and road transfers, and prepare clothing for humid forests, mountains and cities. Any changes to geography also require reconsideration of entry documents, transit and actual payment terms. It would be misleading to promise unchanged services and prices when reducing an eight-country journey to three.

## Frequently asked questions about nature tours featuring Brazil, Peru and Colombia

### Is this itinerary suitable for a multi-day trek to Machu Picchu?

Our [32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) includes a sightseeing visit to Machu Picchu. A multi-day trek is not specified.

### Can it be described as a three-country journey?

This is a multi-country programme featuring those three alongside five others. A separate three-country trip requires a different itinerary and a recalculation of logistics.

### Which part of the journey demands attention to altitude?

Primarily the highland sections of Bolivia and Peru, including Titicaca and Cusco. Wellbeing and physical demands should be assessed individually.

### Where can I find alternative nature itineraries?

Compare the [general multi-country nature selection](/multi-country/interests/nature/) and [Peru nature tours](/interests/nature/tours/peru/) if you would like to spend more time in the Andes.

lead: >-
  The Wildlife and Safaris filter includes a 32-day journey in which Brazil, Colombia and Peru are only three of eight countries. Tijuca, Iguazu, Guatapé, the Andes and Titicaca are on the route, but dedicated wildlife watching is not included in the selected three countries. Sea excursions with opportunities to observe island fauna take place in Ecuador, in the Galápagos.
---

## Where wildlife is actually observed on this itinerary

For the combination of Brazil, Colombia and Peru, the Wildlife and Safaris theme requires us to distinguish between exploring landscapes and organised outings to observe wild animals. These are different experiences. The catalogue includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} whose main route features all three countries and whose complete programme carries a wildlife-interest tag. The tag, however, applies to **the entire tour**, not automatically to each country.

The current selection features a [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Besides Brazil, Colombia and Peru, it visits Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Ecuador. The three countries named on this page form a selected subset of the longer route, not a separate three-country itinerary or a promise of direct flights between them.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

| Country | Nature-related section |
|---|---|
| Brazil | Tijuca Forest and Iguazu Falls |
| Colombia | Guatapé rock and reservoirs |
| Peru | Andes, Titicaca and mountain valleys |

This table describes **actual stops**. It does not suggest that safaris, birdwatching or animal-search excursions are included in all three countries.

## Brazil: Atlantic Forest and Iguazu

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the route goes up Corcovado through [Tijuca National Park](/brazil/place/tijuca-national-park/). This reveals the green mountain landscape above the metropolis, but the excursion primarily features the statue of Christ and the city panorama. The tour does not promise a separate expedition to observe birds in Tijuca.

The principal nature visit in Brazil is [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). A group excursion with a Russian-speaking guide explores the Brazilian side of the falls. The waterfalls are surrounded by subtropical Atlantic Forest, a valuable protected ecosystem whether or not any particular animal is seen. Along the route, visitors encounter wet observation paths, dense vegetation, spray and changing views of the cascades.

Bird enthusiasts can add the [Bird Park](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/) **for an extra charge**. This involves visiting purpose-built aviaries, not searching for free-living birds along forest trails. Another optional activity, Macuco Safari, combines a forest-road section, a short walk and a boat ride near the waterfalls. It is also paid for separately. The distinction matters: the base tour includes Iguazu sightseeing, but not both optional activities.

## Colombia: impressive landscapes without a promised safari

The Colombian stage begins after Ecuador. The current itinerary includes [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), a trip to [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and [El Peñón rock](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/), followed by [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) and [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/).

The Guatapé trip offers views of green slopes and reservoirs. However, the specified eight-hour excursion also features settlements, architecture and regional roads. It contains no separate promise of encountering rare birds or animals. Cartagena and Bogotá are presented through cultural and urban tours, not national parks.

Anyone choosing Colombia primarily for its wildlife should therefore discuss **a separately arranged addition to the itinerary**, rather than expecting unspecified animal encounters between city tours. The particular region, season, availability and content of such an addition must be agreed individually. The existing [catalogue of journeys featuring Brazil and Colombia](/multi-country/brazil_colombia/) shows possible routes, but each wildlife activity needs to be checked against the day-by-day programme.

## Peru: mountain geography, Lake Titicaca and Inca heritage

The Peruvian section comes after high-altitude Bolivia. Travellers cross the border near Desaguadero, visit [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), explore the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/) and travel by bus through La Raya Pass to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/). An excursion to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and a trip to Lima follow.

Here, nature is experienced through altitude, changing vegetation, open plateaus and mountain valleys. Yet the main organised activities involve Uros culture, stops at historic sites, sightseeing at Machu Picchu and city walks. **Observing Andean wildlife is not listed as a separate product.** Even if travellers see birds or llamas along the way, such chance encounters cannot be treated as an included service.

Altitude is a practical concern: the itinerary reaches Peru after traversing the highlands of Chile and Bolivia, only then arriving in Puno and Cusco. Those stages cannot be rearranged casually when designing a shorter trip. Appropriate acclimatisation time and a discussion of individual restrictions are needed before booking.

## Where island wildlife encounters are planned on the same tour

A major feature of the full itinerary is that after Peru, travellers fly to **Ecuador** and then to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). On [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), the programme explores the highlands and lava tunnels. The following day offers a sea excursion **on one of two alternative routes**: North Seymour with Bachas Beach or South Plaza with Cape Carrión.

Depending on the confirmed route, there may be opportunities to observe seabirds, sea lions and iguanas, as well as snorkel. The tour does not include both alternatives together or guarantee sightings of every species. Special visitor rules apply on the islands' protected areas: stay on permitted paths, keep your distance from animals and follow authorised guides' instructions.

This explains why the Wildlife and Safaris filter includes the full eight-country journey even though cultural visits predominate in Colombia and Peru. If island fauna is a priority, compare [tours combining Peru and Ecuador](/multi-country/ecuador_peru/) and [multi-country wildlife journeys](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/).

## Choosing a route: scenery or wildlife

For waterfalls and forest landscapes, focus on the time allocated in Brazil. For mountains and cultural excursions, Peru offers the most relevant stops. For planned wildlife watching, the most substantial confirmed section of this particular tour lies in the Galápagos, **in Ecuador**.

If you have less than 32 days, we can discuss shortening the route, but the programme would need to be rebuilt: preserve the essential nature days, choose flights, check authorised excursions and distinguish included activities from optional ones. The price and services of the complete eight-country itinerary do not automatically carry over.

## Frequently asked questions about wildlife in Brazil, Colombia and Peru

### Is the Bird Park visit at Iguazu included?

No. The base programme includes a group excursion on the Brazilian side of the falls. The [Bird Park](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/) and Macuco Safari are optional extras at additional cost.

### Is there a wildlife safari in the Colombian section?

No such safari is included in the confirmed itinerary. The Colombian section covers Medellín, Guatapé, Cartagena, Bogotá and Zipaquirá. A dedicated nature addition must be arranged separately.

### Do travellers visit Machu Picchu and Titicaca?

Yes. Both are included in the [32-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). They reveal Peru's mountain geography and culture, but are not a guaranteed animal-watching programme.

### Are the Galápagos part of the three-country combination on this page?

No. Ecuador is an additional country on the longer tour, outside the selected three. It is where the island nature excursion takes place. When choosing, account for all eight countries and confirm which of the two Galápagos alternatives applies.

In our catalogue, these four countries feature on an extensive 32-day route through eight countries. Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and Ecuador lie between the named destinations: choose by considering the full sequence, not merely the four names in the filter.

## How four countries are connected within one journey

[Brazil](/brazil/) occupies the opening section: São Paulo, [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) with Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain, then [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The Argentine section follows. From Buenos Aires, the itinerary features a one-day ferry excursion to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), returning to Argentina.

The route then passes through Santiago and the Atacama in Chile, high-altitude Bolivia and Uyuni. Only then does the [Peru](/peru/) section begin: Lake Titicaca, [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). Peru is followed by Quito and the Galápagos in Ecuador. The finale is [Colombia](/colombia/), including Medellín, Cartagena and Bogotá.

This is how the [32-day tour through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) is organised. The four countries in the selection title are **part of a larger journey**, not a ready-made four-country tour. The programme also includes Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and Ecuador; omitting these sections would require a new flight plan.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Brazil and Uruguay: why Argentina lies between them

Rio and Iguazu offer two very different Brazilian experiences: a major oceanfront city and a natural waterfall complex on the border. The route then crosses to the Argentine side of Iguazu and continues to Buenos Aires. Uruguay can thus be visited without another international flight: travellers take a ferry to Montevideo.

This is a one-day excursion returning to Buenos Aires, **not a series of overnight stays on the Uruguayan coast**. The programme introduces Montevideo's old town and central squares. Actual time in the capital depends on the ferry schedule, check-in and border formalities.

Two entries are especially relevant: first into Uruguay, then **re-entry into Argentina** after the return ferry. Staying in Uruguay for several days would mean changing not only hotels, but also the timetable for the subsequent Chilean section. Compare [Brazil and Uruguay itineraries](/multi-country/brazil_uruguay/) and [tours in Uruguay](/uruguay/tour/).

## Peru after Bolivia: altitude, archaeology and tickets

Peru follows the high-altitude Chile–Bolivia crossing. The itinerary includes Puno and the Uros Islands on Titicaca, a tourist bus across the Andes to Cusco, an excursion to Machu Picchu, Inca monuments and a final flight to Lima.

These demands differ fundamentally from city sightseeing in Montevideo or a walk through Rio. Travel and excursions at altitude call for attention to wellbeing, gradual acclimatisation, hydration, warm layers and insurance terms. Discussing high-altitude travel with a doctor in advance is particularly sensible for those with heart or lung conditions or concerns about altitude tolerance.

For [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), the exact entry circuit matters. Peru's Ministry of Culture divides visits into several routes; a ticket for one does not provide access to every viewpoint. For a private itinerary, agree on the preferred experience and ticket first, then arrange the train, transfers and onward flight around it.

This is more complex than spending “a couple of days in Peru en route to Colombia.” Even with fewer countries, Cusco, Machu Picchu and Lima require a substantial block of time.

## Colombia at the end: Medellín, Cartagena and Bogotá

After the Ecuadorian section, travellers arrive in [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). The programme includes a trip to El Peñón rock and Guatapé and a visit to Comuna 13. Next comes [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) on the Caribbean coast, followed by [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), Monserrate and an excursion to Zipaquirá's Salt Cathedral.

This is not just one stop “in Colombia” but three distinct urban settings. In and around Medellín, the terrain and excursions outside the city matter. In Cartagena, there are walks through the historic centre and hot coastal weather. Bogotá is high in the Andes, so evenings call for different clothing than on the Caribbean coast.

The Colombian section includes domestic flights. When creating a shorter four-country itinerary, choose which of the three cities are essential rather than reducing every visit to a few hours. The [Colombia tours catalogue](/colombia/tour/) offers other options.

## Weather and luggage: four different requirements

| Stage | What to prepare for |
|---|---|
| Rio and Iguazu | Warmth, humidity and a rain jacket |
| Montevideo | Coastal wind and a light jacket |
| Titicaca and Cusco | Cold hours, sunshine and altitude |
| Cartagena and Bogotá | Heat by the sea and cooler Andean weather |

These are clothing guidelines, not a forecast for an entire country. The full route also includes the Atacama Desert, Bolivia's highlands and the Galápagos Islands. Your luggage must work for sunny city walks, waterfall humidity and cold early-morning departures at altitude. Check baggage allowances for each domestic flight separately; they can differ from those on the international journey.

Our tour includes accommodation in 4-star hotels and domestic flights, while international flights are paid for separately. Excursion formats vary: some are group tours and others private. Do not apply the conditions of one specific excursion automatically to all 32 days.

## Entry rules, payments and medical preparation

Requirements must be checked for **all eight countries on the actual itinerary**, not only those in the filter. For ordinary Russian passports, Uruguay's Ministry of the Interior indicates short visa-free entry, but that does not answer questions about re-entering Argentina, airline transit rules or travellers of other nationalities. Entry conditions, permitted border crossings, passport validity and children's documents must be reviewed for every country in the tour sequence.

The selected four countries use the Brazilian real (BRL), Uruguayan peso (UYU), Peruvian sol (PEN) and Colombian peso (COP). Other currencies apply in the other countries on the itinerary; Ecuador uses the US dollar. A budget quoted in USD helps compare prices but does not ensure that dollars will be accepted locally. Check fees, whether your particular bank card works and an agreed backup payment option.

According to the WHO, yellow fever activity persisted in parts of South America in 2026. Risk depends on the specific region and type of travel. Discuss medical recommendations, possible vaccination and certificate requirements at subsequent borders with a qualified specialist in advance, and verify current official country rules.

We can help compare flight connections, documentation, ferry times and high-altitude excursions, and agree on a private redistribution of days. We cannot guarantee border-control decisions, medical clearances or the operation of payment instruments.

## What must change if you want only Brazil, Colombia, Peru and Uruguay

The central question is which parts of the longer journey you want to keep. If Rio, Iguazu, Montevideo, Machu Picchu and all three Colombian cities are essential, that already makes for a complex itinerary involving several long-distance flights. If Peru and Colombia are the priorities, fewer urban stops and more time in the Andes can be discussed.

But excluding Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and Ecuador involves more than deleting lines from a programme. The Uruguayan excursion is linked to Buenos Aires, the Peruvian section begins after Bolivia and Colombia follows Ecuador. New arrival and departure points, flights, hotels and pricing are needed. For more options, see [all multi-country journeys](/multi-country/).

## Frequently asked questions about Brazil, Colombia, Peru and Uruguay

### Is there a ready-made tour visiting only these four countries?

No. Our catalogue features a 32-day journey through eight countries. A trip limited to the four selected nations needs to be planned separately.

### How much time is spent in Uruguay?

On the current programme, Montevideo is visited during one day from Buenos Aires, with a return to the same city. There is no overnight stay in Uruguay.

### Can I travel from Peru to Colombia without Ecuador?

Different flight logistics can be discussed for a private itinerary. On the published tour, Quito and the Galápagos lie between these countries, so a direct transfer is not part of the existing programme.

### Are all the excursions private?

No. The [full itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) specifies both group and private excursions, a tourist bus and domestic flights. The format depends on the particular day.

### What should I check before paying?

The full eight-country route, border crossings including re-entry into Argentina, Machu Picchu tickets, your health's tolerance of high altitude and which services are excluded. International flights are not part of the quoted tour price.

lead: >-
  Brazil, Colombia, Peru and Uruguay feature in a 32-day journey through eight countries. Within these four, the main active experiences involve views of Iguazu, Colombia's mountainous terrain and the trip from Cusco to Machu Picchu. Uruguay offers a one-day city excursion. The high-altitude jeep section takes place in other countries on the full itinerary, so it should not be presented as a separate programme within these four.
---

## How the adventure itinerary through Brazil, Colombia, Peru and Uruguay works

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. On the [existing “Eight South American Countries in 32 Days” programme](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), the four selected countries are joined by Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and Ecuador. **The four countries are part of this itinerary, not a separate ready-made tour.**

The adventure experiences vary in their physical demands. Brazil offers walks along viewpoints at tropical waterfalls and Rio's mountain panoramas; Peru has high-altitude transfers and a trip to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/); Colombia offers [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/), its rock and the mountainous shores of its reservoir. Uruguay is represented by a trip to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), which is not in itself a sporting adventure.

## Brazil: Iguazu and Rio's scenic ascents

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the itinerary includes Corcovado, Christ the Redeemer, Tijuca Forest and Sugarloaf Mountain. For Corcovado, the programme specifies a special train; for Sugarloaf, a cable car via Urca. These provide an introduction to the city's terrain and panoramic views, **not a planned mountain trek**.

On the [Brazilian side of Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), travellers follow sightseeing paths beside the waterfalls. Macuco Safari, combining a journey through the forest with a motorboat ride near the water, is available **as a paid optional activity**. Decide whether to add it based on your willingness to get wet, potential weather restrictions and the operator's conditions for the date. Its exclusion from the base price matters when comparing [adventure tours in Brazil](/interests/adventure/tours/brazil/).

## Peru: the Andes, a bus over the pass and Machu Picchu by train

In the Peruvian section of the long itinerary, Puno, Lake Titicaca, [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) follow the Bolivian border crossing. Between Puno and Cusco, a tourist bus makes stops in Andahuaylillas, Raqchi, Sicuani, at La Raya Pass and in Pucará. La Raya Pass stands at approximately 4,400 metres: even when the main distance is covered by vehicle, altitude remains a significant factor for wellbeing.

The visit to Machu Picchu occupies a sightseeing day: a group excursion with an English-speaking guide, a train journey back to Cusco, with lunch included. **We do not promise a multi-day hike along the Inca Trail.** The terraces, stone buildings and mountain scenery make a strong impression without a trekking approach, but the nature of the visit must be assessed from the actual excursion, not from the “Adventure” label in the filter.

Travellers seeking a sporting route on foot should distinguish this extensive sightseeing tour from dedicated [adventure programmes in Peru](/interests/adventure/tours/peru/). For high-altitude stages, a gentle pace in the first days, spare time between transfers and a discussion of individual health limitations with a professional are advisable.

## Colombia: El Peñón and Guatapé without an invented ascent

After flying to [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), travellers head towards El Peñón de Guatapé rock, a replica of old El Peñol, the town of [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and its reservoir. The excursion with an English-speaking guide lasts eight hours. Panoramas, historic streets, mountainous scenery and a visit to the rock are confirmed, but **a specific ascent of the staircase is not listed as an included service**.

The journey is particularly interesting after Peru's highlands: in Colombia, the emphasis moves from archaeological monuments and long mountain-bus travel to hills, reservoirs and urban districts. City tours of Medellín and Comuna 13, [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) and [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) follow. This section does not include independent rafting, mountaineering or a multi-day hike unless separately confirmed as an additional service.

## Uruguay: why one sightseeing day matters when planning

Uruguay is visited from Buenos Aires on this eight-country itinerary: an early transfer to the port, a ferry to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), sightseeing in the capital with an English-speaking guide and a return crossing the same day. This is a significant logistical undertaking, but the walk itself focuses on urban landmarks: the port, Independence Square, the [Old Town](/uruguay/place/montevideo-old-town/) and the cathedral.

If your main aim is to spend as many days as possible on nature trails and in the mountains, including Uruguay adds another country and a cultural stop. If seeing very different parts of South America matters, the one-day crossing broadens the geography without a long standalone Uruguayan stage. You can also compare the [full catalogue for this country combination](/multi-country/brazil_colombia_peru_uruguay/).

## The altitude and main off-road experience also lie outside these four countries

The most technically demanding active section of the same complete tour runs **through Chile and Bolivia**: San Pedro de Atacama, high-altitude lagoons and a two-day 4×4 off-road journey to Uyuni. Parts of the route exceed 4,000 metres, where altitude sickness is possible. This does not turn Brazil, Colombia, Peru and Uruguay into a standalone sequence of off-road activities; to understand the physical demands, read the [full eight-country route](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/).

## Frequently asked questions about adventures across four countries

### Is multi-day trekking to Machu Picchu included?

No, not on the programme described. It includes a one-day excursion and a train journey back to Cusco. This is a way to discover the monument, but not an Inca Trail hike.

### Do I need to prepare for high altitude?

Yes. The complete itinerary includes high-altitude sections above 4,000 metres in Bolivia and La Raya Pass in Peru. Allow time to adapt, and discuss your wellbeing and personal medical limitations in advance.

### Is Macuco Safari at Iguazu already paid for?

No. On this tour, it is listed separately from the main excursion and costs extra. Confirm the conditions of the chosen activity before travelling.

### Is the Montevideo trip an adventure activity?

It is an intensive sightseeing day involving a ferry crossing, but its content is cultural and urban. No separate active-sport programme in Uruguay is confirmed here.
